newsitem.title: USA: US High Court to decide scientific testimony case.
newsitem.headline: US High Court to decide scientific testimony case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court said Monday it would hear an appeal by three companies and decide on the standard to be used by appellate courts in reviewing a judge's decision on excluding expert scientific testimony.
The justices agreed to hear the appeal by General Electric Co, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Monsanto Co.
The case involved a lawsuit seeking damages on behalf of Robert Joiner, an electrician who was diagnosed in 1991, at the age of 37, with lung cancer.

Joiner acknowledged his smoking and his family's history of lung cancer may have predisposed him to developing the disease. But he claimed his exposure to polychlorinated biphenyls and other chemicals while working for Thomasville, Georgia in repairing electrical transformers served to promote his cancer.
The three companies made the various chemical compounds in the power transformers.

A U.S. appeals court in 1996 reversed a judge's decision to exclude testimony by two experts linking lung cancer to the chemicals in the transformers. The appeals court was applying a 1993 Supreme Court decision.
The appeals court said the judge had improperly evaluated the correctness of the experts' opinions rather than just judging whether the foundations for their beliefs were sound.
The companies said different appeals courts have applied different standards in reviewing trial court judges' decisions to exclude or admit expert testimony.
The justices will hear arguments in the case during its term that begins in October, with a decision likely early next year.
